# NVIDIA (NVDA) analysis, as of 15 Nov 2026

**Summary:** NVDA closed at **$162.85** on 13 Nov 2026, its lowest close in 52 weeks. It is down about 21% in two weeks and trades at its lowest trailing multiples in Equibles' history (back to 2020): **20.6× P/E and 19.4× EV/EBITDA**. The main reason is that Jensen Huang has left as CEO. An Equibles 8-K summary says he resigned as President, CEO and director on 11 Nov 2026. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and Harvey C. Jones is the first Board Chair. The business was still growing fast at the last report: revenue of $96B, more than double the prior year, and a 70% growth outlook for FY2028. Q3 FY27 results are expected next week.

Each figure is tagged **[EQ]** for Equibles or **[FD]** for Financial Datasets. I used **14 Equibles requests**.

---

## 1. Price, performance and valuation

**Price [EQ]**
- Close $162.85 on 13 Nov, down 2.0% on the day. Market cap is $3.92T and EV is $3.90T.
- 52-week closing range is $162.85–$239.24. The intraday range is $148.80 (12 Nov) to $243.37 (6 Oct).

| Period | Return [EQ] |
|---|---|
| 1 week | −12.7% |
| 1 month (from 15 Oct) | −25.0% |
| 3 months | −27.5% |
| 6 months | −27.6% |
| 1 year / year to date | −12.5% / −12.5% |

**The selloff [EQ]:** the stock closed at $206.69 on 3 Nov and fell to $181.60 on 5 Nov. On 12 Nov, the day the 8-K was filed, it traded as low as $148.80 and closed at $166.19. Volume that day was 748M shares, about 7× the recent average.

**Valuation [EQ].** Current multiples use the 13 Nov price and trailing figures through 26 Jul 2026 (TTM EPS $7.91, EBITDA $201B).

| Date (earnings point) | P/E | EV/EBITDA |
|---|---|---|
| Feb 2023 (FY23 Q4) | 133.8 | 99.3 |
| Feb 2024 (FY24 Q4) | 56.6 | 48.5 |
| Feb 2025 (FY25 Q4) | 44.7 | 38.0 |
| Feb 2026 (FY26 Q4) | 39.9 | 35.7 |
| Aug 2026 (FY27 Q2) | 26.5 | 25.0 |
| **Now** | **20.6** | **19.4** |

- Forward P/E is **17.5×** on FY27 (year to Jan 2027) EPS of $9.32, from 50 analysts. EV/revenue is 12.9×.
- Equibles' peer group of large semiconductor companies has a median P/E of 44.3× and a median forward P/E of 17.9×.
- Earnings have been growing faster than the share price for three years, so the multiple has kept shrinking. The latest drop is about risk (the leadership change and politics), not weaker profits.

## 2. Segments and margins [EQ]

**Revenue by segment and market ($B, fiscal years end in late January)**

| | FY2024 | FY2025 | FY2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compute & Networking | 47.4 | 116.2 | 193.5 |
| Graphics | 13.5 | 14.3 | 22.5 |
| Data Center (market) | 47.5 | 115.2 | 193.7 |
| – Compute | 39.0 | 102.2 | 162.4 |
| – Networking | 8.6 | 13.0 | 31.4 |
| Gaming | 10.4 | 11.4 | 16.0 |
| Pro Visualization | 1.6 | 1.9 | 3.2 |
| Automotive | 1.1 | 1.7 | 2.3 |
| **Total** | **60.9** | **130.5** | **215.9** |

- Data Center was 90% of FY26 revenue. Networking more than doubled (+142%).
- By region, revenue from China including Hong Kong fell from $25.0B to $19.7B. The US was $149.6B, or 69% of the total.

**Margins**

| | FY2024 | FY2025 | FY2026 | TTM to Jul 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gross margin | 72.7% | 75.0% | 71.1% | — (Q2: 75%, from the call) |
| Operating margin | 54.1% | 62.4% | 60.4% | 65.2% (EBIT) |
| Net margin | 48.8% | 55.8% | 55.6% | — |
| Compute & Networking segment margin | 67.5% | 71.3% | 67.3% | |
| Graphics segment margin | 43.2% | 35.5% | 40.8% | |

- Margins peaked in FY25. The FY26 dip came from the Blackwell launch and costs related to China.
- Gross margin recovered to 75% in Q2 FY27, but management guided it down: 74% in Q3, a low of 71–72% in Q4, then 72–73% in FY28. The reason given was "extreme pricing conditions in memory."
- R&D fell from 14.2% to 8.6% of revenue as sales grew faster than spending.

## 3. Signals

**Insider trades [EQ]** (the last 100 filings, 18 Mar – 4 Nov 2026)
- There were **no open-market purchases**. There were 75 sales of about 7.33M shares worth **$1.59B**.
- Director **Mark Stevens** sold the most: 6.34M shares for $1.39B. That includes 1.356M shares at $219.72 (about $298M) on 18 Sep, which was **not** a pre-scheduled 10b5-1 sale.
- Jensen Huang sold 529K shares for about $99M, and filed gifts of about 118M shares on 18 Mar to indirect holdings.
- Kress sold $35.7M (under a 10b5-1 plan) and General Counsel Tim Teter sold $28.3M.
- The last sale on file was 21 Sep. Since then there have only been director Tench Coxe's monthly 500K-share gifts.

**Largest institutional holders [EQ]** (13F filings as of 30 Sep 2026; 6,145 institutions holding 17.69B shares worth $3.92T). The percentages are each holder's share of all 13F-reported shares, not of all shares outstanding.

| Holder | Shares | Value | % of 13F total |
|---|---|---|---|
| BlackRock | 1.94B | $443B | 11.0% |
| Vanguard Capital Mgmt | 1.54B | $352B | 8.7% |
| State Street | 1.03B | $234B | 5.8% |
| FMR (Fidelity) | 0.93B | $213B | 5.3% |
| Geode | 0.61B | $140B | 3.5% |
| Vanguard Portfolio Mgmt | 0.51B | $117B | 2.9% |
| JPMorgan | 0.46B | $106B | 2.6% |

**Short interest [EQ]**
- 279.6M shares on 30 Oct, with 2.8 days to cover. That is about 1.1% of roughly 24.5B diluted shares.
- It has come down from 311.4M on 30 Sep and 324.1M on 15 Jul. A year earlier it was 232.9M with 1.0 day to cover.
- These numbers predate the CEO news. The 15 Nov report will be the first to reflect it.

**Congressional trades [EQ]** (trailing year): 52 trades, 23 purchases and 29 sales.
- Disclosed purchases total about $0.5M–$1.4M and sales about $1.3M–$6.1M.
- The biggest was Nancy Pelosi's sale of $1M–$5M on 24 Dec 2025, followed by her purchases of $350K–$750K (30 Dec – 16 Jan).
- Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse made 7 sales totalling $233K–$645K. Sen. Markwayne Mullin bought $100K–$250K (29 Dec).
- The most recent was Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar's purchase of $2K–$30K on 23 Oct.

**News [FD]** (latest 10 headlines; the date filters returned the same 10, so I can't see earlier November)
- CNBC: Treasury Secretary Bessent calls for a "dramatic shakeup" and an outside CEO.
- Reuters: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left the company in August 2025.
- Forbes: "NVIDIA Without Jensen Huang."
- MarketWatch: Q3 earnings next week are "one of Wall Street's most anticipated" calls in years.
- I only have the headlines, not the full stories.

## 4. Latest earnings call: Q2 FY2027, 26 Aug 2026 [EQ]

This guidance came from Huang and Kress before Huang left. Kress is now interim CEO.

**Demand**
- Revenue was $96B, more than double the prior year. Data Center was $89B, up 18% from Q1.
  - Hyperscalers: $49B, up 13% from Q1.
  - Other customers (neoclouds, industrial and enterprise): $40B, up 25% from Q1 and 138% from a year earlier.
- Kress said "we are seeing demand acceleration even at our scale." She cited a cloud backlog above $2T and top-five hyperscaler capex of about $800B in 2026 and $1.3T in 2027.
- **Preliminary FY28 revenue growth is about 70%,** while "customers' forecasts point to our growth doubling." Huang: "even though our demand is much greater than 70%, our supply allows us to confidently deliver 70%."
- Q3 revenue guidance is **$108B ±2%**. Vera Rubin started production shipments in August and should be about 20% of Q3 data center revenue. Purchase orders have come from every major hyperscaler, AI cloud and OEM.
- NVIDIA's revenue per gigawatt of data center capacity has grown from about $18B (Hopper) to $25B (Blackwell) and about $40B (Vera Rubin).

**Supply**
- Kress: "we expect supply to remain a bottleneck, at least through the end of fiscal year 28." Huang: "our entire supply chain is challenged," including memory, power, construction, cooling and labor.
- Inventory rose to $32B ahead of the Rubin ramp. Memory scarcity is pushing up costs, which drives the margin guidance in section 2.
- China: less than 1% of data center revenue came from Hopper shipments to China, and the outlook assumes **no** China data center revenue.
- **Financing exposure to watch:** NVIDIA said it has invested about $50B in frontier AI labs and set up $500B+ financing platforms with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone and others. It also offers take-or-pay and revenue-sharing deals to neoclouds and credit support for about 2 GW for one lab.

---

**Takeaways**
- The business grew fast through mid-2026, and management's limit on growth was supply, not demand.
- The stock now carries a leadership and political-risk discount, at about 17.5× forward earnings.
- The Q3 report and call next week, the first under Kress, will test whether the $108B guide and the 70% FY28 outlook still hold.
- Risks to weigh against the low multiple: heavy insider selling with no purchases, guided gross-margin declines, and NVIDIA's growing role in financing its customers.
